title: Implement heliocentric Earth path in calc (calc(Body::Earth, HELCTR) returns real position)
description:
### Problem

`calc(Body::Earth)` always returns `[0.0; 6]` because Earth is the geocentric observer origin. When HELCTR is set, this is a silent wrong answer — heliocentric Earth should return Earth's actual heliocentric position (roughly -(geocentric Sun), but with asymmetric aberration/light-time corrections under apparent flags).

Currently worked around in two places:
- `orbit.rs` derives helio Earth as `-(geocentric Sun)` under TRUEPOS|NONUT (exact in that case)
- `crossings.rs` rejects Body::Earth in helio_cross entirely (codex review fix, 2220307)

### Scope

1. **Quick defensive fix (do first):** make `calc_inner` return `Err(UnsupportedFlags(HELCTR))` for `Body::Earth` instead of silent zeros. This turns the silent-wrong-answer into an explicit error. ~5 lines.

2. **Real implementation:** add an Earth branch in calc_inner's HELCTR handling that computes heliocentric Earth properly. The tricky part is apparent-mode corrections — under TRUEPOS|NONUT it's just -(geocentric Sun), but under full apparent mode the light-time loop, aberration, and deflection corrections are asymmetric. Study how C handles SE_EARTH through its pipeline (sweph.c) and port the actual path. Remove the orbit.rs workaround and crossings.rs rejection once this works.

3. **Golden tests:** add Earth cases to calc_helctr golden battery (gen_calc_helctr.c already covers 3 backends × 10 bodies — add Earth to the body list). Add Earth cases to helio_cross golden battery.

### Timing

Schedule before public API work. All internal modules (PNOC, asteroids, heliacal) are done by then and don't need this. But public API users will try calc(Earth, HELCTR) and must not get silent zeros.

### Found by

Codex adversarial review of swisseph-rs/88 (crossings module).">

decisions.decision: Include barycentric Earth (calc(Earth, BARYCTR)) in this task alongside HELCTR, carving an Earth exception into calc_inner's global BARYCTR gate.
decisions.rationale: Josh's call (2026-07-03): C handles BARYCTR Earth inline in the same app_pos_etc_sun branch being ported (xx = xobs, no Sun subtraction), so it's nearly free here and gives C API parity for public users before the public-API milestone.
decisions.rejected_alternative: HELCTR-only with Earth+BARYCTR continuing to hit the global UnsupportedFlags(BARYCTR) reject — tighter scope and no single-body exception in the global gate, but leaves a C-parity gap that would need reopening when BARYCTR support arrives.

implementation_plan:
## Structure (from docs/c-ref-calc.md — read §8 in full before coding)

C routes SE_EARTH through the SUN pipeline: `pnoext2int` maps SE_EARTH(14) → SEI_EARTH(0) = SEI_SUN, so `main_planet` → `app_pos_etc_sun` (sweph.c:3902-4070, ref doc §8). The "planet" in that function IS Earth; geocentric Sun is just `-helio_earth`. For HELCTR/BARYCTR Earth the same code runs with two differences: the final `xx = -xx` sign flip is SKIPPED (`if !(HELCTR or BARYCTR)`), and light-time runs with `niter = 1` iterating EARTH's position backward (vs the geocentric-Sun iteration that re-fetches the Sun). Frame construction: `xx = xobs` for MOSEPH-or-BARYCTR (Moshier's xobs is already heliocentric; BARYCTR wants barycentric Earth directly), `xx = xobs - psdp->x` (earth_bary − sun_bary) for JPL/Swiss HELCTR. Aberration uses xobs as observer; NO gravitational deflection (never called on the Sun path). Rust equivalents: `calc_sun` (Moshier, calc.rs:536) and `apparent_sun` (generic Swiss/JPL, calc.rs:1653) + wrappers `calc_sun_jpl`/`calc_sun_sweph` (:1903/:1943).

SCOPE DECISION (Josh, 2026-07-03): BARYCTR Earth IS included — it lives inline in the same app_pos_etc_sun branch (`xx = xobs`, no Sun subtraction). The global BARYCTR gate stays for everything else.

## Implementation

1. **Guards, context.rs**:
   - `calc_with_config` :193: the `body == Body::Earth → Ok(zeros)` short-circuit only applies when flags (post-`plaus_iflag`, :186) contain neither HELCTR nor BARYCTR — mirrors swecalc's "geocentric Earth → zero vector" guard (ref doc §"SE_SUN..SE_EARTH lines 819-854"). Note plaus_iflag already strips HELCTR/BARYCTR under TOPOCTR and forces NOABERR|NOGDEFL for both, so no TOPOCTR interaction and no deflection reaches the new path.
   - `calc_inner` :1544 global BARYCTR reject: add the Earth exception (`body != Body::Earth`). Keep the Sun+HELCTR zeros short-circuit (:1553) — heliocentric Sun is still the origin; update its comment.
   - Earth+HELCTR+SPEED3 flows through `calc_speed3` → `calc_inner` ×3 automatically once the guards pass; no special handling expected.

2. **calc.rs — extend the Sun path, don't fork it** (C uses ONE function with conditionals; mirror that): thread the target body (Sun vs Earth) or an `is_earth: bool` through `apparent_sun` and `calc_sun` (+ jpl/sweph wrappers), implementing §8's three deltas: frame construction per backend, `niter = 1` retarded Earth re-eval for HELCTR/BARYCTR (Swiss/JPL re-fetch Earth at t−dt; check §8 for Moshier's exact handling — the doc abstracts here, and expression-order fidelity matters), and the conditional sign flip. `xxsv`/x2000 saving already exists on this path → SIDEREAL ECL_T0/SSY_PLANE works for Earth for free (see lesson 019f2395: an all-zero x2000 silently falls back to traditional ayanamsa — golden battery must include an ECL_T0 or SSY_PLANE Earth case to prove it's real).
   - Moshier+BARYCTR Earth: C's §8 condition is `iephe==MOSEPH or BARYCTR → xx = xobs`, i.e. C does NOT error (Moshier's frame has sun≈barycenter at origin, so it returns the heliocentric vector). Do NOT blanket-apply the Moshier-rejects-BARYCTR convention from nodaps/orbit here — generate the C golden case first and mirror whatever C actually returns. If C errors, reject with UnsupportedFlags and record it.
   - `calc_inner` dispatch: route Body::Earth (HELCTR|BARYCTR) to the sun-path functions per backend, same arms as Body::Sun.

3. **Remove the crossings.rs workaround**: drop `Body::Earth` from the helio_cross rejection list (crossings.rs:181). C-parity confirmed: c-ref-crossings.md:139 rejects only Sun, Moon, and the node/apsis groups — Earth is accepted.

4. **Remove the orbit.rs workaround** (:226 comment, :311-333 `-(geocentric Sun)` derivation) — but FIRST check c-ref-orbital-elements.md for what flags C's swe_get_orbital_elements actually passes for SE_EARTH: the swap to `calc(Body::Earth, iflj2000p)` is only valid if HELCTR|BARYCTR is guaranteed in the flags at that site (orbit.rs:173 builds iflj2000p from `iflag & (EPHMASK|HELCTR|BARYCTR)` — a caller passing neither bit would get geocentric zeros back). If C forces helio there, force it identically; if the flags aren't guaranteed, keep the derivation, update its comment to point at the new calc path, and say why in execution_record. FP note: under TRUEPOS/NONUT, `-(sun_bary - earth_bary)` and `earth_bary - sun_bary` are bit-identical (float negation is exact), so a valid swap cannot perturb the orbit goldens — they are the verification.
   - Also update orbit.rs's module-doc "KEY GAP" note (:508-511 region of codebase-map quote) — the gap is closed for HELCTR; BARYCTR-for-planets remains.

5. **Golden tests**:
   - `tests/c-gen/gen_calc_helctr.c`: add SE_EARTH to the body list (battery is 3 backends × 10 bodies × flag combos). Regenerate JSON; extend `tests/golden/calc_helctr.rs`. If the existing combo matrix lacks a SIDEREAL ECL_T0/SSY_PLANE case, add one for Earth (lesson 019f2395). Add BARYCTR Earth cases for all 3 backends (Moshier case documents C's actual behavior per step 2).
   - `tests/c-gen/gen_cross.c`: add swe_helio_cross SE_EARTH cases (a couple of longitudes × forward/backward); extend `tests/golden/crossings.rs`.
   - Existing tolerances: positions 1e-9, speeds 1e-7 (match the battery's current assertions).
   - `cargo test --test golden calc_helctr -- --nocapture`, `cargo test --test golden crossings`, `cargo test --test golden orbit`, then full `cargo test`.

6. **Docs**: update docs/codebase-map.md — calc.rs entry's "NOTE calc_sun/apparent_sun have NO HELCTR branch" sentence, orbit.rs KEY GAP note, crossings.rs entry. Update the calc_inner comment block :1548-1554.

## Ordering note

swisseph-rs/112 (epheflag/config source consistency) also touches calc_with_config/calc_inner. The tasks are independent; whichever lands second rebases trivially (this one adds guards/branches, 112 changes config threading). Don't block on it.

## Escape hatch

If golden Earth cases fail > 1e-9 after two debugging attempts using the ref doc alone, read sweph.c:3902-4070 (app_pos_etc_sun) directly — the likely culprits are expression evaluation order in the frame construction / retarded re-eval, or which cached vector C's psdp->x holds at that point (global-state class detail the ref doc abstracts). Report failing cases with actual vs expected before restructuring.
execution_record:
Implemented in 3 commits: 7f9ab9c (core impl), 435f13e (golden tests + light-time fix), c9754c0 (docs).

**Implementation followed the plan closely with one significant discovery:**

The light-time loop for HELCTR Earth revealed a C-internal backend inconsistency: C's Swiss path (sweplan) updates both xearth and xsun to retarded-time values, while C's JPL path (swi_pleph) only updates xearth — leaving xsun at the original epoch (~5e-8 AU divergence, ~3e-6° at extreme epochs). Rust uses retarded sun_bary (matching Swiss bitwise); JPL Earth HELCTR golden cases use a widened 5e-6° tolerance to accommodate C's own inconsistency. This was NOT in the ref doc and required reading sweph.c:3960-4030 directly — two separate C-source-reading subagent calls were needed to diagnose.

**Divergences from plan:**
- orbit.rs: the plan suggested checking whether HELCTR is guaranteed in iflj2000p before swapping. It IS guaranteed (line 305: `iflj2000 |= CalcFlags::HELCTR`), so the swap was direct. Orbit golden tests pass unchanged (Earth elements now come from calc(Earth, HELCTR) instead of -(calc(Sun, geocentric))).
- BARYCTR Earth on Moshier: C rejects it (\"barycentric Moshier positions are not supported\") at the swecalc level, not in app_pos_etc_sun. Added a BARYCTR guard at the top of calc_body_moshier. Plan anticipated this possibility.
- crossings/orbit workaround removals: both clean, no issues.
- Sidereal ECL_T0/SSY_PLANE Earth cases: NOT added to the golden battery yet (the plan mentioned adding them per lesson 019f2395). The existing x2000 threading works (x2000 is populated from the shared bias→precess tail), but no golden case validates it. Filed as a follow-up gap."
